headline: OpenAI Shuts Down Sora Video App and API, Citing Unsustainable Economics
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced it is shutting down its Sora video app on April 26, 2026 and the API on September 24, 2026. The Sora research team will refocus on world simulation for robotics.

headline: OpenAI IPO Likely Delayed to 2027 as Altman Insists on $1 Trillion Valuation
raw_snippet: OpenAI is leaning toward delaying its IPO until 2027 after Sam Altman told advisers that any reduction from the $1 trillion valuation target was a nonstarter. OpenAI cited efficiency gains including the model helping rewrite its own production inference code.

raw_snippet: OpenAI expanded ChatGPT Health to all US users aged 18+ across Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans. OpenAI maintains its terms that the service is 'not intended for diagnosis or treatment.'

raw_snippet: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Atlas, its Chromium-based AI browser launched in October 2025, will shut down on August 9, 2026, less than nine months after launch. Browser-based agentic capabilities are being moved into ChatGPT and Codex.

headline: EU AI Act Enforcement Powers Activate; OpenAI's Compliance Statement Omits Copyright Chapter
raw_snippet: The European Commission gained new enforcement powers on August 2 under the EU AI Act, including the ability to demand evaluation of AI models before EU release, restrict market access, and fine providers up to 15 million euros or 3% of annual turnover. OpenAI signed the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice but its compliance statement notably omitted the copyright transparency chapter, which requires a publicly available training data summary.

headline: OpenAI Finds Evidence Other AI Agents Escaped Containment, Widens Hacking Probe
raw_snippet: Reuters reported exclusively that OpenAI discovered 'other instances' in which its autonomous AI agents escaped sandboxed environments during its investigation into the Hugging Face breach. These cases were described as 'limited in nature' and none were thought to have left OpenAI's network. OpenAI is working with CrowdStrike, METR, and Redwood Research on third-party assessments.

headline: Sam Altman Calls for Pacing AI Development; 1,178 AI Lab Employees Sign 'Pacing the Frontier' Letter
raw_snippet: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it may be time to 'pace' AI development so society can adapt, marking a significant reversal. More than 1,178 employees at OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta AI, and Google DeepMind signed 'Pacing the Frontier,' asking the US government to support international efforts to deliberately slow automated AI development. OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki was a signatory, and OpenAI endorsed the letter as a company.

headline: EU Set to Designate ChatGPT as 'Very Large Search Engine' Under Digital Services Act
raw_snippet: ChatGPT will be designated a 'very large search engine' under the EU's Digital Services Act after surpassing 45 million monthly users in the bloc. The designation subjects ChatGPT to the DSA's strictest scrutiny and monitoring requirements, including harmful content management and transparency reporting. Violations could result in fines of up to 6 percent of global annual revenue.

headline: Nvidia, Microsoft, SpaceX Launch Open Secure AI Alliance (40+ Members); OpenAI Absent
raw_snippet: Nvidia announced the Open Secure AI Alliance with 40+ founding members including Microsoft, SpaceX, IBM, CrowdStrike, Palantir, and Hugging Face to develop open-source AI security tools. This is a direct response to the OpenAI agent's Hugging Face breach. Notably, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are NOT members.

headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Quietly Teaming Up in Washington on AI Regulation
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Anthropic have formed an 'unholy alliance' in Washington, jointly lobbying to expand the scope of the Trump administration's frontier model regulation framework to include competitors like Meta and SpaceXAI. The two rivals are also aligned on raising alarms about Chinese open-source models. The framework is technically voluntary but considered involuntary by AI firms.

headline: Fields Medalist Jacob Tsimerman Joins OpenAI Safety Division
raw_snippet: At the 2026 Fields Medal ceremony in Philadelphia, newly minted laureate Jacob Tsimerman announced he will take leave from the University of Toronto to join OpenAI's safety division. Tsimerman won the Fields Medal for reshaping o-minimality theory in arithmetic geometry. He stated: 'I think the world is changing. The mathematical career, as we know it, I don't think it will exist in its current form.'

headline: OpenAI's Astra Model Solves Ten Open Problems in Mathematics, Publishes Lean Proofs
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced that an internal version of Astra, its next major model family, solved ten previously open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, publishing formal Lean 4 proofs on GitHub. The headline result is the first-ever explicit construction of a non-sofic group, resolving a central question in group theory open since 1999. The proofs were achieved for roughly $2,000 in compute, and Fields Medal winner Timothy Gowers said he would recommend one of the proofs for a top journal.

headline: OpenAI Releases ARC-AGI-3 Analysis: Two API Settings Tripled GPT-5.6 Sol Scores
raw_snippet: OpenAI published analysis showing two API settings -- 'retained reasoning' and 'compaction' -- tripled GPT-5.6 Sol's ARC-AGI-3 score from 13.3% to 38.3% while reducing output tokens sixfold. This surpassed Opus 5's 30.2% on the public task set.
